raw_response.overlap_rationale: Both full texts are accessible and share two co-authors (Hug March and David Saurí), a broader geographical setting (Barcelona/Catalonia, Spain), and funding from the same Spanish CICYT grant (CSO2009-12772-C03-01 / CSO2009-12772-03-01). However, they investigate completely distinct historical eras, institutional actors, and empirical datasets with zero sample overlap. Study A (Gorostiza, March & Saurí 2013) is a historical archival study of the retail utility Sociedad General de Aguas de Barcelona (SGAB) under worker collectivization during the Spanish Civil War (1936–1939), drawing on 1936–1940 company correspondence (12 archival boxes, ~8,000 documents), 1930s press clippings, municipal proceedings, and two interviews with retired SGAB workers. Study B (March & Saurí 2013) is a contemporary political-economic and fiscal study of regional water governance in Metropolitan Barcelona and Catalonia (primarily 2000–2012), analyzing how EU environmental directives and regional water-tax financing drove public debt at the Catalan Water Agency (ACA) and bulk supplier Aigües Ter-Llobregat (ATLL), leading to the 2011–2012 private leasing tender of ATLL, using 2000–2011 Catalan/ACA budgets, ATLL policy reports, statistical series, and 2011–2012 press reports.
raw_response.study_a_sample_and_data: Historical archival case study of the collectivized Barcelona Water Company (Sociedad General de Aguas de Barcelona, SGAB) in Barcelona, Spain during the Spanish Civil War (1936–1939). Primary data comprise SGAB archival correspondence from 1936–1940 (12 boxes, ~8,000 documents), SGAB annual reports (1936–1939), Barcelona City Council and Generalitat official proceedings/decrees (1930–1938), 1930s press clippings (La Vanguardia, Solidaridad Obrera, Luz y Fuerza), and N = 2 interviews with retired SGAB workers conducted in 2009 and 2011.
raw_response.study_b_sample_and_data: Contemporary institutional and fiscal case study of the regional water cycle in Metropolitan Barcelona and the Inland Basins of Catalonia, Spain (focusing on 1999–2012, with wastewater plant series 1973–2009 and budget/debt/tariff series 2000–2012). Units of analysis are regional public water agencies—Agència Catalana de l'Aigua (ACA) and bulk supplier Aigües Ter-Llobregat (ATLL)—analyzed via ACA annual budgets and reports (2000–2011), ATLL policy reports, Catalan government budgets and decrees, statistical databases, and 2011–2012 newspaper and trade-union/official statements.
